brief: Goldman Sachs TMT specialist Peter Callahan previews the firm's Communacopia and Technology Conference in San Francisco and gives the desk's read going in. The chain he draws: TMT fundamentals improved through 2Q earnings, with NVDA guiding FY27 revenues above 70% y/y and AVGO pointing to over 100% growth in 2027 and 2028, but price action did not follow. The GS TMT 12-month Momentum Pair fell more than 10% in August as semis lagged both the broader market and software. He attributes the gap to a complicated macro backdrop ahead of a live FOMC meeting this month and muted risk appetite across volumes, vol and gross exposures, which leaves investors debating what else is needed to re-engage the AI trade or whether the market is signalling a regime shift away from the capex trade. The rest is a subsector temperature check and a list of debates rather than an argument: semis most loved, software bifurcated between inference economy names and SaaS apathy, internet choppy, telcos bid on positioning, cable out of favor. Sector views are reported as desk sentiment and GIR previews, not as Callahan's own directional calls.
